text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Security forces, besieging hundreds of "terrorists" from the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) gathered in congress, have so far killed more than 90 gunmen. GIA chief Antar Zouabri might be among the trapped men in an area near Attatba in Blida province, south of Algiers. Hundreds of GIA rebels had came to the group base there from Algiers and other regions to attend a congress to plot ways to step up their activities.
- The National Assembly (lower house) to resume session on Tuesday to vote the house ruling bodies and its internal regulation.
- The government sets up a task force to end anarchy prevailing at wholesale vegetable and fruit markets.
- Algiers's Zmirli hospital received about 600 violence casualties so far this year.
- Tizi-Ouzou court has acquitted a former deputy prosecutor at Blida court charged with belonging to armed groups and "apology for terrorism".
